title: A worker crashes mid-batch: what a queue and a log do next
captions: A queue, like Amazon SQS. Worker 1 receives 4 messages. They stay in the queue, but other workers cannot see them for the visibility timeout: 30 seconds by default.
Worker 1 handles m1 and m2 and deletes each one. Then it handles m3, but it crashes before it can delete it.
After 30 seconds, m3 and m4 are visible again. Worker 2 receives them, so m3 runs twice. m1 and m2 are deleted, so they are gone for good.
A log, like one Kafka partition. Each message has an offset: 0, 1, 2 and so on. The group's committed offset is 0, so Worker A reads from offset 0.
Worker A handles offsets 0, 1 and 2. It plans to commit after the batch, but it crashes first. The committed offset is still 0.
Worker B, in the same consumer group, takes over the partition. It starts at the committed offset, so 0, 1 and 2 run again. Nothing was deleted. The log keeps every message until retention ends.
Both systems lost nothing, and both ran some work twice. That is at-least-once delivery. Your handler must be idempotent.
